answer.note: All four ref files hold the same generic text, so I chose the refs from the code. I did not run any tests. D (dogwhistle/honest.py) is the match. Its `_verify_history` (lines 175-184) rejects `prereg_commit == ledger_commit` ("ledger seal must be a separate commit"). It also requires `git diff --name-only` to equal only the public seal file. I did not check that honest.py has two arms. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) has a same-named `_verify_history` (line 191) but has neither check. It is the closest sibling and the likeliest near-miss, so it is a useful contrast. It is also the one I'm swapping in for B. A (study.py) and B (heldout.py) each have a `verify_history` that checks prereg, seal and ledger ancestry and that published digests match. Neither rejects equal commits or restricts the changed files. That differs from the incoming handoff, which listed B and D; I replaced B with C. Suggested 60-minute split: D 35 min (check that the diff is taken against the right base commit, and whether the check should compare the seal commit to the ledger commit), C 12 min, B 7 min, A 6 min.

I did not check that honest.py has two arms. C (dogwhistle/visibility.py) has a same-named `_verify_history` (line 191) but has neither check. It is the closest sibling and the likeliest near-miss, so it is a useful contrast. It is also the one I'm swapping in for B. A (study.py) and B (heldout.py) each have a `verify_history` that checks prereg, seal and ledger ancestry and that published digests match. Neither rejects equal commits or restricts the changed files. That differs from the incoming handoff, which listed B and D; I replaced B with C. Suggested 60-minute split: D 35 min (check that the diff is taken against the right base commit, and whether the check should compare the seal commit to the ledger commit), C 12 min, B 7 min, A 6 min.
